rationale:
bugs_open/301, fix candidate 1 — the one the bug file prefers and the filing lane explicitly offered to whoever takes it (vigilant_designer_offer_analysis HANDOFF_2026-08-18: 'Take bugs_open/301').

THE PROBLEM, plainly. page-build-handler's owned-page refusal lives only in save_page_sections — the LAST step that touches the page. So a build item aimed at a pages.rebuild_policy='owned' page spawns page-content-writer (an LLM call), runs the internal-link-resolver, and is only THEN refused. The work is done and thrown away. bugs_open/301 measured 39 discarded chains in ~2.5 hours on one site. Re-verified live 2026-08-19 post-roll (v1.0.1314): the 10:18 UTC cluster shows a page-build-handler orchestration created 10:18:27 ending complete_error with a COMPLETED page-content-writer child (spawned 10:18:42) and COMPLETED internal-link-resolver child (10:19:16) beside it. [MEASURED 2026-08-19] 146 open findings on owned pages are routed at handler_agent='page-build-handler' right now — each is a guaranteed wasted chain under the current ordering, on a fleet that hit its Anthropic cap on 2026-08-14.

THE FIX. rebuild_policy is knowable the moment load_page_record (step 2) has loaded the page row; it is not consulted until step 12. This change adds ONE opt-in config key to the load_page_record action — refuse_owned_page, absent and therefore inert everywhere — and one migration (488) that names it on page-build-handler's load_page_record step and routes that step's error to mark_item_failed. When the key is set and the loaded page is owned, the action: (1) decides via pageIsOwnedForGuard, the estate's SINGLE ownership predicate (unified for bugs_open/208 at the council reuse_agent seat's own insistence — this change adds no second predicate); (2) files the same deduped owned_page_review row the save-path guard files, refused_by='load_page_record' (emitOwnedPageReviewItem, same item_key namespace, ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING, so it converges with reconcile's and save's rows); (3) returns an error LEADING with ownedPageSkipReasonPrefix — the exact marker update_work_item_status' owned_page_refusal_status (migration 480, live on v1.0.1314) matches in __step_error.message. The refusal therefore lands wont_fix, not failed, with ZERO new vocabulary: it composes with Tier 1 by construction, answering that submission's own risk 5 ('a reviewer should confirm the marker survives whatever step 301 moves the refusal to' — it leads the new error).

THE SAVE-PATH GUARD STAYS. It is the backstop for every other caller and for the early guard's fail-open window; removing it would re-open bugs_closed/295. The early guard fails OPEN on an unreadable policy, matching the predicate's posture — and cheaply here, because unlike the assemble-seam guard (which is the last line before a git commit and therefore logs its fail-open to agent_error_log), this one has the save guard downstream: an unchecked page costs at most one wasted chain, never a clobber.

THE STRUCTURAL CLAIM THAT LICENSES THE MOVE, and how it is being verified. Every content-writing path in page-build-handler's live workflow ends at save_page_sections. Read from the live agent_definitions row 2026-08-19: the only write path is validate_content -> save_sections -> update_status -> spawn_rerender_agent -> deploy_page (rerender/deploy sit AFTER the save, success arm only), and the non-write arms — check_page_found else, mark_no_ready_sections, mark_writer_skipped — park the item without touching the page. So an early refusal refuses exactly the population the save guard refuses today; it cannot cut off a legitimate owned-page write because the workflow contains none. The bug file's '74 completions on owned pages' is NOT counter-evidence: rebuild_policy is MUTABLE and those joins are query-time (the 277 lane's §8 correction — classify by the guard's error text, never the policy column), and the current graph has no bypass. A 090 diagnosis run was filed on exactly this question before this submission (intake 7281193f-59c2-489a-a9f2-fd4d58408cf5, run dd61df1b-0d93-46e6-9065-1e0b9623379a); its verdict will be read and recorded in the lane NOTES, and refutes-if-wrong the central premise.

WHY AN OPT-IN FIELD, AND THE CONSUMERS ENUMERATED RATHER THAN ASSERTED (owner rulings 2026-08-02 §2 and 2026-07-29 §3). [MEASURED 2026-08-19] exactly TWO live, non-snapshot, non-deleted agent_definitions carry a load_page_record step: page-build-handler and tool-recreation-handler. The second is the tool pipeline — the legitimate owner of owned pages, which must NEVER refuse them. That census is what forces the opt-in shape: a default-ON rule in code would have broken the tool pipeline on its next owned-page rebuild. One migration names one step; migration 488's verify block carries a negative control that ABORTS if any other live step acquires the key. Per the RFC_022 narrowing (owner ruling 2026-08-11): opt-in, unsafe side (OFF = today's waste, not a clobber risk) is the default, zero live consumers name it before the migration that ships with it — not architecture scope; this council round is the right venue.

ONE DECLARATION TRADE-OFF, DISCLOSED RATHER THAN DISCOVERED. The key is declared in the spec's ConfigKeys, not Optional: it is a setting (a boolean read from config, like update_work_item_status' skip_if_missing), not a data reference, and ExtractActionInputs would treat an Optional entry as a path to resolve. The consequence: cmd/config-key-audit --optional-key-budget counts Optional ONLY (its own header: 'ConfigKeys is deliberately NOT counted'), so this key does not move load_page_record's budget count (3 of N=10). If the seat reading this thinks accumulated authority should count ConfigKeys too, that is a fair objection to the BUDGET TOOL and I will file it there — hiding was not the intent, which is why this paragraph exists.

NAMED BEHAVIOUR CHANGES, the honest list. (1) A genuine load_page_record error (DB failure, malformed authoritative id — bugs_open/220's fatal path) now routes error_step -> mark_item_failed: the item dies visibly failed, attempt counted, instead of failing the workflow. This ALIGNS the step with every sibling in this workflow (plan_sections, call_content_writer, save_sections, deploy_page all route there already) and is active from config-apply time on the old binary too. The 220 council's objection to a soft miss was that it routed through the SUCCESS-labelled path with the item untouched; routing through mark_item_failed marks the item failed first, which is the loud behaviour that objection asked for. (2) An owned-page item that would today take a no-op arm (mark_no_ready_sections / mark_writer_skipped, both parking at needs_human_review with a 'the target section was NOT rebuilt' message) is now refused up front: wont_fix + owned_page_review row. Both outcomes are visible parks that the promoter's floor ignores (it counts complete/verified/failed only — read from the live pre_query by the 277 lane 2026-08-18), so the gate arithmetic is unchanged; the refusal is the truer record and carries the fix pointer (spec.fix names apply_section_edit and the tool pipeline). (3) tool-recreation-handler: no change by construction — it does not carry the key, and the migration's negative control keeps it that way.

ORDERING, deliberately order-TOLERANT (no _HOLD, no loaded-gun pending state). Config before binary: LoadPageRecordInputSpec has CheckConfig without StrictConfig, so the old binary logs ONE deduped 'unrecognised config key' warning and ignores it (platform/validation/workflow.go:185-195 warns for non-strict actions, never rejects); only the error-routing alignment activates early. Binary before config: the code is dormant until the migration names the key. 488 is exercised: dry-run applied AND rolled back in one transaction against the live row (both NOTICEs fired), and the already-set guard proven able to fire by a double-apply probe that ABORTED with '488: refuse_owned_page is ALREADY set' — the control could have come out otherwise and did.

WHAT THIS DOES NOT DO, stated because it is the obvious objection. It repairs nothing and unblocks nothing: the ~146 queued findings will be refused CHEAPLY instead of expensively, not fixed. The routes that would fix them are owned elsewhere and deliberately not touched: Tier 2 (finding-to-edit conversion) is with the copy_quality_two_stage exchange, migration 473 (the 184 lane) covers literal_markdown deterministically, and bug 301's candidate 3 (producers should stop filing generic content items against owned pages at all) remains the real upstream repair. This change is the ordering half: stop paying for work the guard then throws away.

=== ROUND 2 — EVERY OBJECTION ANSWERED WITH A MEASUREMENT OR THE COMMITTED CODE. Status first: all five edits are COMMITTED (6be66bceb), migration 488 is APPLIED and ledger-recorded (11:05:25Z), the binary is LIVE on both replicas of the fresh roll (pods 12:15Z; refuse_owned_page PRESENT in /proc/1/exe on both, OWNED_PAGE_GUARD present as the long-lived control, nonsense needle absent), and the mechanism is BEHAVIOURALLY PROVEN in production: 3 owned-page content_rewrite items were refused at load (error text: 'step load_page_record failed: ... OWNED_PAGE_GUARD: page learn-algorithms-...'), all 3 landed wont_fix with result.owned_page_refusal stamped, ZERO page-content-writer orchestrations were spawned in their window — and 6 generic-page builds in the same post-roll window spawned writers normally (they later failed at validate_content for pre-existing content reasons, a step this change cannot touch, at the historical rate of ~25/day). 0 refused_by='save_page_sections' reviews since the roll: the save guard is now backstop-only, as designed. ===

GATING, debug_historian HIGH — 488 omitted the pre-mutation snapshot. CONCEDED, REMEDIATED, AND LOGGED. The applied 488 does not open with snapshot_agent(), which scripts/migration/run-migrations.sh's own header requires for every migration touching agent_definitions (I did not read that header; the miss is logged in WRONG_CALLS.md with exactly that as the cheap check). Remediation, in order of usefulness: (1) the TRUE pre-mutation state was preserved — the full pre-488 load_page_record/workflow steps object was dumped from the live row BEFORE apply (~09:47Z) and is now committed verbatim at docs/agent_docs/docs024_key_docs_latest/bugfix_301_owned_guard_ordering/PRE_488_page_build_handler_workflow_steps.json; (2) a snapshot_agent('page-build-handler', ...) snapshot was taken 2026-08-19 (NOTICE: 'Snapshot captured: type=page-build-handler, source_version=1, source_id=8f35c080...') naming the pre-488 dump in its reason, so the restore chain is discoverable from the DB side too; (3) the exercised ROLLBACK file reverses both keys. 488 itself is deliberately NOT edited: its md5 is in schema_migrations, and editing an applied, ledgered file orphans the ledger row (the documented renumbering trap, same class). The next agent_definitions migration from this lane opens with snapshot_agent().

debug_historian MEDIUM — the row-count guard 'asserted from memory, not baked into the migration'. FACTUALLY ANSWERED BY THE APPLIED SQL, which the sketch elided (my error — the sketch showed only the UPDATE). The applied guard block opens: SELECT count(*) INTO n FROM agent_definitions WHERE type='page-build-handler' AND is_active AND COALESCE(is_snapshot,false)=false AND deleted_at IS NULL; IF n <> 1 THEN RAISE EXCEPTION '488: expected exactly 1 live page-build-handler row, found %'. Your own round-1 check independently confirmed one active v1 row per carrier. The two-active-rows landmine cannot bite this apply.

guardian MEDIUM — the 480-precondition 'stated in prose, not enforced by the verify block'. FACTUALLY ANSWERED BY THE APPLIED SQL, same elision: the guard block RAISEs '488: mark_item_failed does not carry owned_page_refusal_status=wont_fix (has %) — apply/verify migration 480 first, or an early refusal lands failed and poisons the promoter floor' unless the Tier 1 key is present, in the same transaction as the UPDATE. And it is no longer only a static guarantee: the 3 production refusals traversed error_step -> mark_item_failed -> owned_page_refusal_status and landed wont_fix, post-roll, through the live 480 mechanism.

editquality MEDIUM — 'the helper is not shown wired into BOTH return paths'. ANSWERED WITH THE COMMITTED CODE (6be66bceb), load_page_record_action.go: the authoritative-id path reads 'res, err := loadPageRecordByID(ctx, params, siteID, authID, logger); if err != nil { return nil, err }; return refuseOwnedPageIfConfigured(ctx, params, res, siteID, logger)' and the name/id path ends 'res, err := queryPageRecordRow(ctx, params.DB, siteID, pageName, pageIDInput, logger); if err != nil { return nil, err }; return refuseOwnedPageIfConfigured(ctx, params, res, siteID, logger)'. Both terminal returns route through the one helper; the only other return shapes are found:false results (helper no-ops on found:false by design) and errors.

guardian MEDIUM — error_step changes routing for ALL load failures; 'retry/attempt semantics need explicit confirmation, not alignment-by-analogy'. MEASURED, and the answer has three parts. (1) Attempt counting is IDENTICAL: update_work_item_status's UPDATE sets attempt_count = attempt_count + 1 on every status write (v3_site_actions.go:5748-5754), exactly as fail_work_item does. (2) The real divergence is the re-triage ladder: fail_work_item re-triages until max_attempts ('WHEN attempt_count + 1 >= max_attempts THEN failed' — load_work_item_actions.go:1152), mark_item_failed writes terminal failed directly. A genuine load error therefore loses saga-failure re-triage — which is already true of EVERY other step in this workflow (plan_sections, call_content_writer, validate_content, save_sections, deploy_page all route to mark_item_failed; the bug file's 0-of-38 rows all died on that arm). (3) The affected population is measured at ZERO: genuine load_page_record step errors (error naming the step but not the guard) in the live table = 0, against 3 guard refusals; live table only, since the archive drops the error column — a 7-day window, stated as such. The refusal path itself needs no retry ladder: wont_fix releases the dedup key (idx_swi_dedup excludes it), so the finding re-raises on next detection, which is the correct re-entry for a refusal.

bug_historian LOW — no test for the genuine-error routing in isolation. Answered by composition plus production: the routing mechanism is the coordinator's existing routeToErrorStepOrFail (step-level ErrorStep preferred), which the three sibling steps exercise in production daily and which the 3 live refusals traversed end-to-end post-roll (orchestration rows show failed_step=load_page_record, current_step=complete_error, and the items carry the routed error text — the whole arm demonstrably fires). The marker-absent discrimination (a genuine failure stays failed) is pinned by migration 480's own test suite on update_work_item_status, which drives the same block with a non-guard error. And the genuine-error population this could surprise is currently zero (measurement above).

bug_historian LOW — shared-predicate edge cases inherited by both call sites. Acknowledged as designed: one predicate is the 208 council's own requirement (reuse_agent seat), and an edge case in pageIsOwnedForGuard now has two identically-behaving consumers rather than two drifting ones — the failure mode changes from divergence (silent) to shared (visible at either site). The early site's fail-open is additionally cheap: the save-path guard is downstream, so a predicate stand-down costs one wasted chain, never a write.

guardian LOW — shared-binary crash surface for the helper. The helper is comma-ok end to end (config[k].(bool), res.(map), m[found].(bool), m[id].(string)); an unparsable id logs Warn and stands down; the fail-open branch is tested (case 4); and the key-absent test pins that the default path performs NO additional reads — tool-recreation-handler's exact production shape (its live config: site_id + page_name only; refuse_owned_page confirmed '(absent)' post-488, re-read today). Both replicas have run the new binary since 12:15Z with tool-recreation-handler config untouched.

prior_art_librarian HIGH — 'the submission asks approval before its own falsification test resolved'. RESOLVED AND ATTACHED, honestly: the 090 run (dd61df1b) terminated UNVERIFIABLE at its iteration cap — 'Diagnosis NOT confirmed (stopped: iteration-cap). Best-effort trail attached for a human; no fix proposed.' It neither confirmed nor refuted. Recorded in the lane NOTES as promised. What now carries the premise is stronger than either the graph read or the 090 could have been: the production discriminating pair. 3 owned-page items refused at load with zero writer children, 6 generic builds spawning writers normally in the same window, 0 save-path refusals since the roll. If a write path bypassing save_sections existed for owned pages, the pre-roll behaviour could not have been 100% guard-named failures on the MODIFY types (85 of 87 discriminated by error text, bugs_open/301 §corrections), and the post-roll refusals could not be gate-neutral — every consequence the premise predicts has now been observed live.

prior_art_librarian MEDIUM — the two-consumer census 'asserted without an attached check'. ATTACHED, twice: re-run today — SELECT type FROM agent_definitions WHERE is_active AND COALESCE(is_snapshot,false)=false AND deleted_at IS NULL AND default_config::text LIKE '%"load_page_record"%' returns exactly page-build-handler, tool-recreation-handler — and your own round-1 reviewers' check output shows the same two rows with their live config (page-build-handler carrying the key post-apply, tool-recreation-handler without it).

prior_art_librarian MEDIUM — 480's live shape and the marker 'asserted from a single read; could have drifted'. Now production-proven post-roll rather than asserted: the 3 refusals landed wont_fix through the live mechanism after the fresh build. The marker cannot have been renamed between read and ship: the test asserts strings.HasPrefix against the CONSTANT, so a rename fails the suite at build time.

reuse_agent MEDIUM + prior_art MEDIUM — the widening-precedent landmine ('the owned-page guard belongs on assemble_page, NOT git_commit — the wider net breaks the only paths owned pages use'). CITED AND DISTINGUISHED, with the census as the discriminator the seats asked for. That landmine is about attaching the guard to a seam owned pages LEGITIMATELY traverse: git_commit is how owned pages deploy (page-rerender, section-editor), so gating it breaks the legitimate path — the 208 fix chose assemble_page precisely because only the three generic loops use it. load_page_record is a git_commit-shaped seam: tool-recreation-handler (the tool pipeline, owned pages' legitimate builder) traverses it. That is exactly why this change is NOT an in-action rule but a per-step opt-in: the wider net structurally cannot catch the legitimate path, because that path never carries the key — enforced three ways (default OFF in code; 488's negative control RAISEs if any other live step acquires the key; the key-absent test pins that an unflagged caller performs no ownership read at all). The precedent is the reason for the shape, not an overlooked hazard.

editquality LOW — the '146' figure. Re-derived with the split attached, because a single number was the wrong shape: open-status owned-page findings routed at page-build-handler today are failed 84, unresolved 36, needs_human_review 13, detected 9 (142; live table; the figure moves with traffic — it read 146 at 10:50Z, and a narrower status set explains the round-1 check's 64). The cost claim survives at any of these numbers: every one of them that reaches the handler is a wasted chain under the old ordering and a cheap wont_fix under the new one — 3 already avoided in the first hours.

plan.summary: ROUND 2 of c7bc1b9e. Edits unchanged and already committed (6be66bceb), migration 488 applied+ledgered, binary LIVE on both replicas of the 2026-08-19 12:15Z roll, mechanism behaviourally proven in production (3 owned-page refusals at load, wont_fix, zero writer spawns; 6 generic builds spawning writers normally; 0 save-path refusals since). This round answers every round-1 objection with a measurement or the committed code, and remediates the gating snapshot omission (pre-488 state committed verbatim; snapshot_agent taken; WRONG_CALLS logged). page-build-handler refuses an owned page at the LAST workflow step, after the LLM writer and link resolver have already run — 39 discarded chains in 2.5h measured, 146 findings queued behind the same waste today. This change teaches the load_page_record action an opt-in refuse_owned_page key (default OFF, inert everywhere): when set and the loaded page is rebuild_policy='owned', the action files the same deduped owned_page_review row the save-path guard files and errors with the OWNED_PAGE_GUARD marker leading, so the existing error_step -> mark_item_failed -> owned_page_refusal_status machinery (migration 480, live) stamps the item wont_fix. Migration 488 opts in exactly one step — page-build-handler.load_page_record — and routes its error to mark_item_failed. The save-path guard stays as the backstop. Of the two live carriers of this action, the other (tool-recreation-handler, the tool pipeline) never gets the key, enforced by the migration's negative control.

edits.rationale: Declare the new key where the action's config contract lives, so UnknownConfigKeys recognises it and the audit sees it. ConfigKeys not Optional: it is a setting, not a data reference — and the budget trade-off that choice carries is disclosed in the rationale rather than left to be discovered.

edits.rationale: The mechanism. Both return paths (the authoritative-id path and the name/id path) route their found result through one helper, so the check cannot be reached on one path and missed on the other. Reuses the guard's three existing pieces — pageIsOwnedForGuard (the single predicate), emitOwnedPageReviewItem (the same deduped review row), ownedPageSkipReasonPrefix leading the error (the Tier 1 marker) — and adds no new vocabulary anywhere. Fail-open on an unreadable policy, logged at Warn: the save-path guard is still downstream, so the window costs one wasted chain at most, never a clobber.

Four cases, and the discrimination cases are what make it a control rather than a demonstration. (1) Key set + owned page: refused, review row filed, error LEADS with ownedPageSkipReasonPrefix — asserted with strings.HasPrefix against the CONSTANT, so a rename of the marker goes red here rather than silently unstamping wont_fix. (2) Key set + generic page: proceeds, and ExpectationsWereMet proves no review row was filed. (3) KEY ABSENT + owned page: the mock expects ONLY the page lookup — a rebuild_policy read or an INSERT fails the test, pinning that the default path does not so much as read the policy (tool-recreation-handler's production case). (4) Policy read errors: fail-open, record returned, no review row. All pass; the package suite is green.

plan.risks:
1. **The structural claim ('no write path bypasses save_sections') is the load-bearing premise.** It is read from the live workflow graph first-hand, and a 090 diagnosis run (dd61df1b) was filed on exactly this question before submission; its verdict is read and recorded either way. If the loop refutes it, this change is withdrawn or narrowed before the roll — the migration is unapplied-able (ROLLBACK file, exercised) and the Go half is inert without it.

2. **Genuine load errors change route** (workflow-fail -> mark_item_failed, failed, attempt counted). Aligns with every sibling step and satisfies the 220 council's loud-failure intent, but it IS a change to 220's error path: a malformed/deleted authoritative id now lands the item failed via the error arm rather than failing the saga. A reviewer who thinks the saga-failure path carried semantics the item-failure path does not (e.g. a dispatcher retry that only fires on saga failure) should say so — I did not find one.

3. **Owned-page items that today park needs_human_review via the no-op arms will instead land wont_fix + owned_page_review.** Gate-neutral (the promoter floor counts complete/verified/failed only) and truer, but it moves rows between two human-facing queues; whoever drains needs_human_review should not be surprised to see owned-page no-ops disappear from it after the next roll.

4. **The refusal is keyed on the same string marker as Tier 1** — a rename of ownedPageSkipReasonPrefix silently converts early refusals back to failed. Mitigated identically: the test asserts the prefix FROM the constant, and the constant's doc comment (corrected 2026-08-18) lists the matcher set. This change adds a fourth matcher; the comment should gain the line — noted as a follow-up edit in the same commit if a reviewer agrees it is worth the same-file touch (the comment lives in owned_page_guard.go, whose matcher list currently names three).

5. **Dead code risk in the no-op arms**: after this ships, mark_no_ready_sections / mark_writer_skipped can no longer be reached BY AN OWNED PAGE, but remain reachable by generic pages (writer skips, empty specs) — they are not dead and are not touched.

6. **Emission volume**: an owned page whose finding is re-dispatched repeatedly now emits the review item on every early refusal instead of every late one — same rate, earlier; ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING converges to one open row per page, same as today.
